title: How to Hire Warehouse Workers
summary: Hiring warehouse workers doesn’t have to be slow or costly. This guide breaks down how to define roles clearly, set competitive pay, attract candidates through multiple channels, and move from application to onboarding in as little as 48–72 hours. With the right hiring process in place, you can fill shifts faster and reduce costly turnover.
body_text: ‍ Hiring warehouse workers can feel like a race against time. You need reliable, capable staff fast—but rushing the process often leads to mistakes, costly turnover, and missed deadlines. The good news? With the right strategy, you can hire efficiently without sacrificing quality. Top tips to hire warehouse workers: Define the role Set competitive rates Write a simple, attractive job description Use multiple hiring channels Make applying easy Screen quickly Interview & assess practically Hire fast & onboard immediately Reduce turnover Define the role Before posting anything, be specific. This saves time and bad hires. Clarify: Full-time, part-time, seasonal, or temp Shifts (day/night/weekend) Physical requirements (lifting weight, standing, forklifts) Skills needed (picking/packing, RF scanners, forklift certification) Pay range and overtime Warehouse candidates care most about pay, schedule, and stability. Set competitive rates Before posting, ensure your compensation matches the 2026 market. And make sure you pay more than unemployment benefits. The average hourly rate for a warehouse worker currently ranges from $16 to $22 per hour, depending on location and specialized skills (like forklift operation). Write a simple, attractive job description Keep it short and include: Job title (e.g., Warehouse Associate / Picker-Packer ) Pay (hourly range) Shift & location Main duties Requirements (don’t overdo this) How to apply Use our warehouse worker job description example. Use multiple hiring channels Don’t rely on a single job board. Cast a wider net: Employee Referrals: Offer a "referral bonus" (e.g., $250 after 90 days of employment). This is often the highest-ROI source for reliable workers. Staffing Apps: For quick scaling or seasonal peaks, use specialized apps like Instawork.com . Local Community: Post in local Facebook groups, community centers, or trade schools. Use warehouse staffing solutions All of the hiring steps can be expedited with warehouse staffing solutions like Instawork. Make applying easy Top candidates often accept the first solid offer they receive. If your application takes longer than 3–5 minutes, you will lose them. Mobile-First: Ensure the application is easy to complete on a phone. One-Click Apply: Use platforms like Instawork to allow quick submissions. ‍ Remove Friction: Avoid requiring a resume or a cover letter for entry-level roles; use a simple questionnaire instead. Screen quickly You’re screening for attendance, reliability, and safety. Good screening questions: Can you work this shift consistently? Have you done physical work before? Do you have reliable transportation? Are you authorized to work? Consider a same-day phone screen (5–10 minutes). Essential Skills to Look For: Physical Stamina: Ability to lift (often 50+ lbs) and stand for long shifts. ‍ Technical Literacy: Familiarity with Warehouse Management Systems (WMS) or handheld scanners. ‍ Soft Skills: Reliability, punctuality, and clear communication are often more valuable than specific experience. ‍ Safety Consciousness: A proven track record of following OSHA or site-specific safety protocols. Interview & assess practically Keep interviews short. What to focus on: Past attendance history Comfort with physical work Willingness to follow safety rules Attitude Optional: Basic physical test (if legal in your area) Forklift test or certification check Check our warehouse worker interview questions . Hire fast & onboard immediately In warehouse hiring, speed is often the deciding factor between filling a shift and starting the process all over again. Strong candidates don’t stay available for long, especially during peak seasons. Aim for an “Apply-to-Offer” timeline of 48–72 hours by streamlining each step: Pre-screen quickly: Use a short phone or text screen to confirm availability, shift fit, and work eligibility. Limit interviews: One focused interview is usually enough for entry-level warehouse roles. Prepare offers in advance: Have pay rates, start dates, and shift details ready so you can extend an offer immediately. Same-day onboarding when possible: Completing paperwork, safety training, and shift assignment right away reduces drop-off. The faster you move, the fewer candidates you lose to competing employers—and the sooner your warehouse stays fully staffed. Reduce turnover (this saves money) High turnover is one of the biggest hidden costs in warehouse operations. Every early exit means rehiring, retraining, and lost productivity. To reduce churn: Set clear expectations upfront: Be honest about physical demands, shift schedules, and productivity goals. Match workers to the right shifts: Many early quits happen due to schedule mismatches, not performance. Pay fairly and consistently: Competitive wages and predictable overtime policies build trust. Prioritize safety and training: Workers who feel safe and supported are far more likely to stay. Provide early feedback: A quick check-in during the first week can prevent small issues from becoming reasons to quit. Even modest improvements in retention can significantly lower hiring costs and improve team morale over time. In summary Whether you’re hiring seasonal warehouse staff or permanent team members, speed and clarity are key. Define roles clearly, streamline applications, and screen effectively. Even with some inevitable turnover, a strong hiring process ensures your warehouse stays productive. For faster results, consider staffing solutions that connect you with qualified workers immediately.

title: Navigating EPR Legislation in the U.S.: How Adhesives and Packaging Can Meet Regulations
summary: Explore U.S. EPR packaging regulations and discover how adhesives enable compliance and sustainable solutions.
body_text: The U.S. recycling system has long relied on taxpayers and municipalities to cover the costs of waste collection and processing. Although this model is underperforming, with only about 21% of recyclable material being recycled and most losses occurring at the household level. To address these gaps, policymakers are increasingly adopting Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) laws on a state-by-state level. EPR is already established in regions like the EU and Canada. Now, U.S. states are adopting similar laws to improve collection, recycling rates, reduce waste, and promote sustainable packaging design. For brands and packaging producers, this shift presents both a challenge and an opportunity. Overview of EPR Legislation for Packaging in the U.S. EPR is a policy approach that requires producers to fund and, in some cases, manage the end-of-life of their packaging, including collection, sorting, and recycling, while being incentivized to design packaging that is more easily recyclable and sustainable. This transfers the financial responsibility for packaging waste from local governments to the companies that place packaging on the market. Producers are typically required to join a Producer Responsibility Organization (PRO), also referred to as Stewardship Organizations (SOs), such as the Circular Action Alliance (CAA) , which creates the program plan and manages compliance as well as fee collection. The EPR program plan outlines how fees are assessed and charged to producers. These fees are typically based on the amount and packaging material placed on the market and are eco-modulated, meaning that they vary according to the sustainability attributes of the packaging, such as recyclability, use of recycled content, and design choices. Now at the beginning of 2026, seven states — Oregon, Colorado, California, Maine, Minnesota, Maryland, and Washington — have already adopted EPR packaging laws. Additional states, including New York, New Jersey, Illinois, and Massachusetts, are actively considering similar measures. Each law varies, but the core goal is the same: hold producers accountable for packaging waste. Each law defines “producer” differently, but in most cases, responsibility lies with the company putting the product on the market such as the brand owner, manufacturer, importer, or distributor. If your company sells packaged products in these states, it is essential to determine whether you are a producer under EPR legislation. Products included are defined by legislation or producer responsibility plans and specify packaging types, such as paper products, plastic packaging, e-commerce and food service ware. Some states also include industrial B2B packaging. Definitions vary by state and typically indicate format and material type. Failure to comply can result in penalties, higher costs, and reputational risks. On the other hand, proactive companies can benefit from reduced compliance risks, access to eco-modulated fee incentives, and stronger sustainability credentials. Adhesives: An Important Factor in EPR Packaging Compliance Adhesives and coatings play a critical role in packaging recyclability and are essential to EPR compliance. While they are not recycled, they must be compatible with recycling processes, either removable or integrable without compromising material quality and recycling yields. At H.B. With our testing facilities at headquarters in Willow Lake, MN, USA, and in Blois, France, we test and confirm our adhesives perform well during recycling, separating cleanly from materials to support our customers with sustainable packaging design. Furthermore, we are members of the Association of Plastic Recyclers (APR) and have APR recognized adhesives for PET warp-around labeling. In addition, we collaborate closely with the Fiber Box Association (FBA) and testing institutes to certify our adhesive solutions on customer paper and board packaging. title: 7 Steps to a Winning Return to Office Strategy
summary: Build a return to office strategy that works for your team with these 7 practical steps for a smooth, flexible, and positive transition back to the workplace.
body_text: The purpose of the office has fundamentally shifted. It's no longer the default place for work; it's a destination for specific activities like collaboration, mentorship, and team building. This shift presents a unique opportunity to be intentional about how your team works together. Instead of trying to go back to the way things were, you can design a better future of work. A forward-thinking return to office strategy is your roadmap for this change. It helps you define the role of your physical workspace and create an environment that supports a thriving, flexible, and connected team for the long haul. Key Takeaways Lead with listening and transparency : Build your RTO plan collaboratively by asking for employee feedback through surveys and open forums. Clearly communicate the why behind your decisions and be prepared to adapt based on what you learn. Make the office a destination, not an obligation : Acknowledge that the office needs to offer something more than a home setup. Structure a flexible hybrid model and use in-person time for specific, high-value activities like team collaboration and culture-building. Equip your team with seamless technology : Remove logistical headaches with user-friendly tools for booking desks and meeting rooms. Prioritize software that integrates directly into your team's existing workflow, like Slack or Teams, to ensure high adoption. What is a Return to Office Strategy (and Why You Need One) Bringing people back to the office isn't as simple as unlocking the doors and turning the coffee machine back on. After a long stretch of remote work, employees have new expectations about flexibility and what the office is actually for . Simply demanding everyone show up on a Monday morning without a clear plan is a recipe for confusion and frustration. That's where a return to office (RTO) strategy comes in. An RTO strategy is your company’s game plan for transitioning employees back to a physical workspace. It’s not just a memo with a start date; it’s a thoughtful approach that considers everything from new hybrid schedules to health protocols and office layout. It’s about creating a work environment that people genuinely want to be a part of. Without a solid strategy, you risk losing great people and seeing a drop in morale and productivity. A well-crafted plan, on the other hand, can make the return a positive and energizing experience for everyone. What an RTO Strategy Actually Is At its core, a return to office strategy is a detailed plan that outlines how, when, and why employees will come back to the office. It’s about thinking deeply about the purpose of your physical workspace in a new, flexible world. This isn't just about logistics; it's a chance to redefine how your team collaborates. Your plan should cover new policies, communication channels, and the tools you'll use to manage a more dynamic workplace, like a hybrid work software solution. It answers the big questions so your team doesn’t have to guess, ensuring the transition is smooth, organized, and intentional. Why a Clear Plan Matters for Your Business A clear RTO plan does more than just get people back to their desks—it builds trust. When you communicate your strategy effectively, you address employee concerns head-on and create a sense of security. Everyone knows what to expect, which reduces anxiety and helps maintain productivity. A thoughtful plan also shows your team that you value them by being flexible and reasonable. By implementing tools like a hot desk booking system , you give employees autonomy over their in-office days. This kind of consideration fosters a positive culture, which is essential for keeping your team happy and engaged for the long haul. What to Include in Your Return to Office Plan A successful return-to-office plan isn’t just a memo with a start date. It’s a thoughtful strategy that balances business goals with employee needs. Think of it as a blueprint for your company’s next chapter. A great plan covers how you’ll communicate changes, what flexibility you’ll offer, how you’ll keep everyone safe, and what tools you’ll use to make it all work smoothly. Getting these four pillars right will build trust and make the transition feel less like a mandate and more like a collaborative effort. A Framework for Clear Communication Effective communication is the backbone of your entire RTO strategy. Your team needs to understand not just the what , but the why behind your decisions. Be transparent about your goals for bringing people back and the timeline you have in mind. Use multiple channels—like company-wide meetings, dedicated Slack channels, and regular email updates—to keep employees informed and engaged. This isn’t a one-and-done announcement; it’s an ongoing conversation. Creating a clear framework for communication shows respect for your team and helps manage expectations, preventing confusion and rumors from filling the information gap. Flexible Work Options The nine-to-five, five-days-a-week model is a thing of the past for many companies. The most successful RTO plans embrace flexibility. This could mean letting employees work from home a few days a week or giving teams the autonomy to decide their own in-office schedules. The key is to offer options that support a healthy work-life balance. When you give people some control over when and how they come to the office, they’re more likely to feel valued and motivated. A well-designed hybrid work software can help you manage these new schedules without adding administrative headaches. Health and Safety Guidelines Your team’s well-being should be your top priority. Before anyone returns, you need clear health and safety guidelines in place. This goes beyond just cleaning protocols. Think about office layout, air circulation, and clear policies for what to do when someone feels unwell. The best way to address concerns is to ask your employees what would make them feel comfortable. Running a simple survey can provide valuable insights and show your team that you’re listening. When people feel that their safety is taken seriously, they can focus on their work with peace of mind. The Right Tech and Office Setup A frustrating office experience will send people right back home. To make the return worthwhile, you need the right technology. Smart workspace solutions are essential for making a hybrid office run smoothly. This means implementing tools that make it easy for employees to collaborate and be productive, no matter where they are. A hot desk booking system eliminates the morning scramble for a spot, while easy-to-use meeting room software prevents scheduling conflicts. The goal is to remove friction and make the office a hub for seamless collaboration. Common Roadblocks in Your RTO Rollout Rolling out a return-to-office plan is a big move, and it’s completely normal to hit a few bumps along the way. Even with the most thoughtful strategy, you’re managing a major change in how your team works and lives. The key isn’t to avoid every single problem, but to anticipate the common ones so you can handle them with confidence. From employee hesitation to the logistics of a smaller office, these challenges are a natural part of the process. Let’s walk through the most frequent roadblocks and how you can clear the path for a smoother transition. Handling Employee Pushback and Concerns It’s almost a guarantee that some employees will be hesitant about returning to the office. After years of adapting to remote work, concerns about commutes, flexibility, and work-life balance are valid. The best way to address this is to listen—really listen. Instead of mandating attendance, shift your focus from presence to performance. You can build a culture of trust by asking for and acting on employee feedback . Send out anonymous surveys, host open forums, and encourage managers to have one-on-one chats. When your team sees you’re taking their worries seriously and offering practical solutions, they’re more likely to feel respected and get on board. Working with Limited Space and Resources Many companies downsized their office footprint, which can make the idea of bringing everyone back feel like a complicated puzzle. If you’re working with less square footage, you can’t expect things to run the way they did before. This is your chance to get creative. Smart workspace solutions are essential for making a hybrid office work. Instead of assigned seating, you can implement a hot desking system where employees book a desk through an app before they come in. This ensures everyone has a guaranteed spot and helps you manage office capacity without the chaos, turning your limited space into an efficient, flexible hub for collaboration. Solving Tech Integration Headaches The last thing your team wants is another clunky piece of software to learn. If your RTO tech is difficult to use or doesn’t play well with the tools your team already relies on, adoption will be a struggle. Your return-to-office tools should simplify the process, not complicate it. Look for solutions that integrate with existing platforms like Slack or Microsoft Teams. When employees can book a desk or a meeting room using a tool that’s already part of their daily workflow, the friction disappears. Clear communication is also key; make sure everyone knows how the new tech works and where to go for help. Coordinating a Hybrid Team Managing a team where some people are in the office and others are remote can be tricky. How do you make sure collaboration happens naturally? How do you avoid creating a divide between in-office and remote employees? The goal is to make the hybrid experience feel intentional, not accidental. Using hybrid work software helps everyone see who is planning to be in the office and when. This empowers teams to coordinate their in-person days for brainstorming sessions or project kick-offs. By providing tools that give visibility into office schedules, you help your team make the most of their time together while keeping everyone connected and productive. How to Get Your Team On Board with the RTO Plan Rolling out a return-to-office plan isn't just about sending a memo and expecting everyone to show up. A successful transition depends entirely on getting your team's buy-in. If you approach it as a strict, top-down mandate, you’re likely to face resistance, lower morale, and a dip in productivity. The key is to make your team feel like they are part of the process, not just subject to it. By focusing on collaboration, clear communication, and genuine care for your employees' needs, you can turn a potentially stressful change into a positive step forward for the whole company. It’s about creating an office environment that people want to come back to. The following steps will help you build that trust and enthusiasm, ensuring your RTO plan is something your team can get behind. Involve Employees in the Planning The most effective way to get people on board with a new plan is to give them a voice in creating it. When employees feel heard, they develop a sense of ownership over the outcome. Start by asking for their input through anonymous surveys, small focus groups, or open-door sessions with leadership. Ask them what they need to be productive in the office, what their biggest concerns are, and what a successful hybrid model looks like to them. The goal is to build a culture of trust by showing that you’re not just collecting feedback for show—you’re genuinely using it to shape a better, more inclusive policy for everyone. Use Data to Guide Your Decisions While employee feedback is essential, you should also ground your strategy in objective data. Making decisions based on gut feelings alone can lead to a plan that doesn't fit how your teams actually work. A data-driven approach helps you understand office usage patterns, peak collaboration days, and which teams benefit most from in-person time. Tools that track office attendance and space utilization can provide clear insights, helping you optimize your office layout and schedule. This information allows you to create a flexible plan that meets the real needs of your workforce, rather than one based on assumptions. Prioritize Health and Safety For many employees, the biggest hesitation about returning to the office revolves around health and safety. You can ease these concerns by being transparent and proactive. Clearly communicate the measures you’re taking, whether it’s enhanced cleaning protocols, improved air filtration, or providing more space between workstations. It's vital to keep your team informed about these safety measures to build confidence in the organization's commitment to their well-being. Making safety a visible and ongoing priority shows your team that you value their health, which is fundamental to making them feel comfortable coming back. Give People a Reason to Come In The modern office has to compete with the convenience of working from home. To encourage people to make the commute, you need to offer something they can’t get from their living room. Think about what makes in-person work special: spontaneous collaboration, team-building lunches, mentorship opportunities, and dedicated focus time away from home distractions. You can incentivize employees to return by making the office a hub for connection and culture. Frame office days around specific, valuable activities that strengthen team bonds and drive innovation, turning the workplace into a destination rather than an obligation. How to Build a Flexible RTO Approach A successful return to the office isn’t about flipping a switch back to the way things were. It’s about creating a new way of working that blends the best of both worlds. A flexible approach acknowledges that your team has built new routines and values autonomy, while also recognizing the need for in-person connection and collaboration. The goal is to build a strategy that feels less like a mandate and more like an invitation. Instead of a one-size-fits-all policy, think about creating a framework that can adapt to different roles, teams, and personal circumstances. This shows your employees that you trust them and value their well-being, which is fundamental to a positive company culture. When you give people a say in how and where they work, they’re more likely to be engaged and productive. The right hybrid work software can help you manage this flexibility without adding administrative headaches, making it easy for everyone to coordinate their office days. Explore Hybrid Schedules and Models There’s no single "right" way to do hybrid work. The best model for your company depends on your goals, your culture, and the nature of the work your teams do. Some companies opt for a fixed schedule, where everyone comes into the office on the same core days to maximize face-to-face collaboration. Others prefer a more flexible model, allowing employees or teams to choose which days they come in. Take some time to weigh the pros and cons of each. A fixed schedule can simplify planning and guarantee that people will be in the office together, but it offers less autonomy. A flexible schedule provides more freedom but requires better coordination tools to ensure people are connecting effectively. The key is to find a balance that supports both individual focus and team collaboration. Plan a Phased Return Asking everyone to return to the office five days a week overnight is a recipe for resistance. A sudden change can be jarring, disrupting the routines your employees have built over a long period. Instead, plan a phased return that gradually reintroduces office days. You could start with one or two optional days per week and slowly increase the frequency over a few months. This approach gives everyone time to adjust their personal lives, from arranging childcare to figuring out new commute patterns. It also gives you, as a company, the chance to test your new office setup, gather feedback, and make adjustments before you’re at full capacity. A gradual rollout shows that you’re being thoughtful and considerate, which can make a huge difference in how your RTO plan is received. Accommodate Different Team Needs Your engineering team likely has very different collaboration needs than your sales team. A rigid, company-wide policy can stifle productivity by forcing teams into a model that doesn’t fit their workflow. A better approach is to empower team leaders to work with their members to decide what makes the most sense for them. Start by asking for input. Use surveys and team meetings to understand what your employees need to do their best work. Some teams might benefit from having a dedicated "collaboration day" in the office each week, while others might only need to come in for specific project kickoffs or events. By accommodating these different needs, you show your team that you trust their judgment and are committed to setting them up for success. Use Hot Desking and Flex Spaces If your team isn't in the office every day, you probably don't need a dedicated desk for every employee. This is where hot desking becomes a game-changer. By allowing employees to book a desk when they plan to come in, you can manage your office space much more efficiently. It ensures everyone has a guaranteed spot to work without the cost of maintaining rows of empty desks. Implementing a flex office software solution makes this process seamless. When employees can book a desk, find a colleague, or reserve a meeting room directly within the tools they already use, like Slack or Teams, the barrier to coming into the office is significantly lower. This simple tech solution supports a flexible RTO by making the office experience easy, predictable, and user-friendly. Tech That Makes Your RTO Easier A successful return-to-office plan isn’t just about policies and schedules; it’s about creating an experience that’s seamless and supportive for your team. The right technology is the backbone of that experience. It removes the little daily frictions that can make coming into the office feel like a chore and instead helps your workplace run like a well-oiled machine. When your team can easily find a desk, book a room, and coordinate with colleagues, they can focus on doing their best work, not on office logistics. Think of your tech stack as the invisible infrastructure that makes hybrid work, well, work. Instead of adding more complexity, the goal is to simplify. The best tools are the ones that feel intuitive and fit right into your team’s existing workflow. From managing who’s in the office on any given day to understanding how your space is actually being used, technology gives you the clarity and control needed to build a flexible and effective RTO strategy. With the right hybrid work software , you can create an office environment that people genuinely want to be a part of. Desk Booking and Space Management Tools In a hybrid model, you can’t just assume there will be a desk for everyone who decides to come in. That uncertainty is a major source of stress for employees. Desk booking systems eliminate the guesswork. These tools allow your team to reserve a workspace in advance, so they know exactly where they’re going before they even leave the house. For office managers, this technology is a game-changer for space management. You can see at a glance how many people are coming in, prevent overcrowding on popular days, and ensure your office resources are used efficiently. A good hot desk booking system provides the flexibility employees want while giving you the oversight you need to manage a dynamic workplace. Easy Meeting Room Booking One of the biggest reasons to bring people back to the office is for in-person collaboration. But that collaboration can’t happen if your team spends half an hour wandering the halls looking for an empty meeting room. Clunky booking processes, double-booked rooms, and confusion over availability can quickly derail a productive day. This is where a streamlined meeting room booking software comes in. When employees can quickly and easily find and reserve a space for team huddles or client meetings, you remove a significant barrier to collaboration. It ensures that when your team makes the effort to come in, they have the resources they need to connect and work together effectively, making their time in the office feel valuable and well-spent. Tools That Work with Slack and Teams The last thing your team needs is another app to download, another password to remember, and another platform to check. This is often called "tool fatigue," and it’s a real obstacle to getting your team to adopt new processes. The most effective RTO tech is the kind that meets your employees where they already are: in communication hubs like Slack and Microsoft Teams. When your desk and room booking tools are integrated directly into these platforms, the process becomes effortless. Employees can book a desk or see who’s in the office with a simple command, right in the same place they chat with colleagues. This approach dramatically increases adoption rates and helps improve team synchronization and visibility. Explore integrations that make office management a natural part of your team’s daily digital routine. Track Attendance and See What's Working How do you know if your RTO strategy is actually working? You can’t rely on assumptions. Data is your best friend when it comes to refining your approach and making sure your office space truly serves your team’s needs. Tools that track office attendance and space utilization give you concrete insights into how your workplace is being used. Are Tuesdays consistently the busiest day? Is one neighborhood of desks more popular than another? This information is vital. It helps you make informed decisions about everything from staffing and resource allocation to future real estate needs. By tracking attendance and gathering employee feedback, you can move from guessing what your team wants to knowing what they need, allowing you to adapt your strategy for long-term success. How to Communicate Your RTO Plan Effectively A great return to office plan can fall flat without a solid communication strategy to back it up. How you share the news, listen to feedback, and manage expectations is just as important as the policy itself. The goal isn't just to inform your team but to bring them along on the journey, making them feel heard and valued. Clear, consistent, and empathetic communication can make the difference between a smooth transition and a rocky one. Think of it as an ongoing conversation, not a one-time announcement. By being open and responsive, you build the trust needed to make your new hybrid model a success for everyone. Be Transparent About Expectations Clarity is your best friend when rolling out an RTO plan. Avoid vague language and be direct about what’s changing and why. Clearly outline the new schedule, in-office days, and any core hours. Most importantly, explain the reasoning behind these decisions. Are you aiming for more collaborative time? Is it about strengthening company culture? When employees understand the "why," they're more likely to get on board. Create a central FAQ document that answers common questions about everything from booking a desk to new safety protocols. Keeping everyone informed and engaged from the start prevents confusion and shows respect for your team's need for information. Gather and Act on Feedback Communication should always be a two-way street. Your team’s perspective is invaluable, so create clear channels for them to share their thoughts. You can use anonymous surveys, town hall Q&A sessions, or dedicated Slack channels to collect feedback. The most critical step? Acting on what you hear. When you make adjustments based on employee input, you build a culture of trust and show that you’re listening. This simple act can significantly improve return to office morale and make people feel like they have a stake in the process. Ignoring feedback is worse than not asking for it at all, so be prepared to make changes. Address Concerns Before They Grow Anticipating your team's worries allows you to address them proactively before they turn into larger issues. Common concerns often revolve around commuting costs, work-life balance, and health and safety. Create a space where people feel comfortable raising these points without fear of judgment. This could be through one-on-one meetings with managers or open-door sessions with HR. By encouraging open communication, you can understand employee needs and preferences and incorporate them into your plan. A well-managed hybrid work software can also help by giving employees the autonomy to manage their schedules, easing anxieties about flexibility and control. Keep the Conversation Going Launching your RTO plan is the beginning, not the end, of the conversation. Treat your strategy as a living document that can evolve. Schedule regular check-ins to discuss what’s working and what isn’t. Share data on office usage and team productivity to keep everyone in the loop. When you make adjustments, communicate them clearly and explain why. This continuous feedback loop shows your team that you’re committed to getting this right for everyone. Your employees' feedback plays a vital role in shaping your workplace, so make sure they know their voices continue to matter long after the initial announcement. Address These Common Employee Concerns A successful return-to-office plan is less about mandates and more about understanding. Your team will have valid questions and concerns about this shift in their work routine. Addressing these issues head-on shows that you’re listening and that you value their well-being, which is fundamental to a smooth transition. By anticipating their worries, you can build a strategy that feels like a partnership rather than a top-down directive. When you proactively solve for these common points of friction, you’re not just managing a logistical change; you’re building trust and reinforcing a positive company culture where people feel supported. Let’s walk through the four biggest concerns you’re likely to hear and how you can thoughtfully address them. Commutes and Work-Life Balance After months or years without a daily commute, the thought of traffic and travel time can be a major source of stress. The time and money spent traveling to and from work directly impact an employee's personal life and budget. Acknowledge this reality and show you’ve considered it. Offering flexible start and end times can help employees avoid peak rush hour. You could also formalize a plan with hybrid work software that allows teams to coordinate their in-office days, ensuring their commute is for purposeful, collaborative work, not just to sit on video calls at a different desk. Ongoing Health and Safety Worries Even as the world moves forward, health and safety remain a top priority for many employees. It’s crucial to create an environment where people feel safe and protected. This goes beyond simply stating policies; you need to make your safety measures visible and clear. Communicate your cleaning protocols, provide information on air filtration systems, and ensure there’s enough space for those who prefer to maintain distance. Using a data-driven approach to plan your office layout and capacity, rather than just guessing, can also provide a layer of reassurance for your team. Access to the Right Tools and Resources If an employee commutes to the office only to find they can’t find a desk or a quiet place to work, the experience will quickly become frustrating. The office needs to be better than their home setup, with seamless access to the tools they need. This is where technology makes all the difference. Implementing a simple hot desk booking system eliminates the morning scramble for a spot. Similarly, having an easy-to-use tool for booking meeting rooms ensures that collaborative time is efficient and productive, making the trip to the office feel worthwhile. Making Sure Everyone Feels Heard Ultimately, your team wants to know their voice matters. A return-to-office plan that’s created in a vacuum is far more likely to face resistance. Encourage open communication by asking for feedback through surveys, team meetings, and one-on-one conversations. The most important step? Acting on what you hear. When employees see their suggestions being implemented, it builds a culture of trust and shows that you’re all in this together. This collaborative approach helps everyone feel like a valued part of the process, not just a passenger. Is Your RTO Strategy Working? How to Tell Once your return-to-office plan is in motion, how do you know if it’s actually a success? Moving past gut feelings and office chatter is key. A successful RTO strategy isn’t just about getting people back into the building; it’s about creating a work environment that supports your team and your business goals. The only way to know for sure is to measure what matters. By tracking the right metrics, you can see what’s resonating with your team and what needs a second look. This isn’t about micromanaging—it’s about making smart, informed decisions that help you refine your approach over time. Let’s look at four key areas you should be monitoring to gauge the health of your RTO strategy. Define Your Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Before you can measure success, you have to define what it looks like for your company. Relying on assumptions won’t cut it; your decisions should always be backed by strong, useful data . Start by setting clear, measurable KPIs that align with your original goals. These could include office attendance rates, desk and meeting room utilization, or employee retention numbers post-implementation. Are certain teams coming in more than others? Are collaborative projects getting done faster? Having specific metrics allows you to see a clear picture of what’s happening and make adjustments based on facts, not feelings. Measure Employee Satisfaction An RTO plan can look great on paper, but if your employees are unhappy, it’s not working. Employee satisfaction is a critical indicator of your strategy’s success. The best way to gauge this is to ask them directly. Use anonymous surveys, team meetings, and one-on-one check-ins to create a continuous feedback loop. It’s not enough to just ask for opinions; you have to show you’re listening by acting on employee feedback and addressing concerns. When people feel heard and respected, they’re more likely to be engaged and supportive of the new work model, which builds a healthier and more collaborative office culture. Analyze How Your Space Is Used Your office is one of your biggest assets, but many companies don’t have a clear view of how it’s being used. In fact, studies show that fewer than half of leaders actually check their office space utilization. By analyzing space usage , you can uncover powerful insights. Are hot desks near the windows always taken? Is one specific conference room constantly booked? Is the "quiet zone" actually being used for focused work? This data helps you optimize your layout, reallocate resources effectively, and ensure your office is designed to meet your team’s real-world needs, not just your assumptions. Track Productivity and Engagement Productivity isn’t about tracking keystrokes or counting hours at a desk. It’s about results. When evaluating your RTO plan, look at team- and project-level outcomes. Are deadlines being met? Is the quality of work consistent? It’s also important to consider that different environments work for different tasks. As experts suggest, you should let your plan be guided by where your employees do their best work. Some productivity metrics might even show that focused, individual tasks are better handled at home. A successful hybrid strategy recognizes this and empowers employees to work where they’ll be most effective, fostering both productivity and trust. Create Your Return to Office Action Plan Putting your strategy into motion is where the real work begins. A thoughtful action plan turns your goals into a clear, manageable process that your team can understand and get behind. It’s about moving from what you want to do to how you’re going to do it, step by step. This is your chance to show employees you’ve listened to their feedback and are committed to a smooth transition for everyone. A well-executed plan minimizes confusion, addresses concerns proactively, and sets the stage for a successful hybrid work environment. Your Step-by-Step Implementation Guide The best way to show your team you value them is by being reasonable and flexible. Start by asking for their opinions through surveys to understand their concerns and preferences. This isn't just about making people feel heard; it gives you valuable data to build a plan that actually works. Next, equip your office with the right tools to make the transition seamless. A clunky system for booking a desk or finding a meeting room will only create frustration. Implementing a user-friendly hot desk booking system that works within Slack or Teams removes friction and makes coming to the office feel easy and efficient, not like a chore. Set a Realistic Timeline Avoid the temptation to flip a switch and expect everyone back in the office overnight. A sudden change can be jarring and lead to pushback. Instead, plan for a gradual return. Start with one or two recommended days in the office and slowly build from there. This phased approach gives your team time to adjust their schedules, figure out new commute patterns, and ease back into the office rhythm. A slow rollout also gives you the chance to test your new setup, gather feedback, and make adjustments before you’re at full capacity. It’s a more human-centered way to manage a big change. Common Pitfalls to Avoid One of the biggest mistakes is relying on gut feelings instead of good data. Guessing what your team wants or how the office will be used can lead to empty offices or overcrowded spaces. Use a data-driven approach by looking at survey results and office usage patterns to make informed decisions. Another common pitfall is a lack of communication. Don't let your employees guess what's happening. Communicate your plans early and often, and create clear channels for feedback. Using hybrid work software can help provide transparency on who is in the office and when, making coordination much simpler for everyone involved. Before you write a single policy, start by listening to your team. The most successful RTO plans are built on a foundation of trust, and that begins with understanding your employees' concerns and preferences. Send out an anonymous survey to get honest feedback on what would make them feel comfortable and productive in the office. This simple act shows you value their input and helps you build a strategy that people will actually get behind. How can we manage bringing people back if we downsized our office? This is a common challenge, but it's also an opportunity to be more intentional with your space. Instead of assigned seating, a hot desking system is the perfect solution. It allows employees to reserve a desk for the days they plan to come in, ensuring everyone has a guaranteed spot without you needing a desk for every single person. This approach turns your smaller office into an efficient, flexible hub that adapts to your team's needs each day. What's the best way to handle pushback from employees who enjoy working remotely? It's important to approach this as a conversation, not a conflict. Acknowledge that their concerns about commutes and flexibility are valid. Instead of focusing on mandates, shift the focus to the purpose of the office. Frame in-person days around specific, valuable activities like team collaboration, brainstorming sessions, or mentorship that can't be replicated over a video call. When the office becomes a destination for connection, it feels less like an obligation. How do we decide on the right hybrid schedule for our company? There is no magic number of days that works for every business. The best hybrid schedule is one that aligns with how your teams actually work. Rather than enforcing a rigid, company-wide rule, consider empowering individual team leaders to decide what makes sense for their workflow. Your sales team might need different in-office time than your engineering team, and that's okay. A flexible approach shows you trust your teams to know how they work best. Do we really need special software to manage a hybrid office? While you could try to manage schedules with spreadsheets and chat threads, you'll quickly find it creates more administrative work and confusion. The right software removes the daily friction that makes coming to the office a hassle. When employees can book a desk, find a colleague, or reserve a meeting room with a simple command in Slack or Teams, the entire process becomes effortless. This not only makes life easier but also gives you valuable data on how your office is being used.

title: A Modern Playbook to Reduce Customer Acquisition Cost
summary: Struggling with high CAC? Learn how to reduce customer acquisition cost with our proven playbook on auditing funnels, optimising targeting, and boosting LTV.
body_text: A Modern Playbook to Reduce Customer Acquisition Cost Mariam Ahmed Co-founder & CTO · January 14, 2026 To bring down your customer acquisition cost, you have to look beyond tweaking individual ad channels. The only way to make a real dent is with a data-driven, full-funnel approach. This means tracking the entire journey, from the first ad someone clicks to their tenth purchase, so you can spot exactly where your budget is being wasted. Real cost reduction comes from understanding how marketing, sales, and retention actually work together. Why Your Customer Acquisition Costs Are Spiralling If your customer acquisition cost (CAC) feels like a runaway train, you’re not alone. Countless e-commerce brands are watching their marketing budgets evaporate with less and less to show for it. The old playbook of just pumping more money into Meta or Google Ads is officially broken. The reasons are a complex mix, creating a brutal environment for any brand trying to grow. This perfect storm is hitting UK businesses particularly hard. Right now, in 2025, customer acquisition costs have shot to all-time highs. Brands are paying up to 222% more for each new customer than they did back in 2013. For many stores on Shopify , that works out to a painful £68-£78 per acquisition. This surge is fed by a nasty combination of economic stagnation—with the UK economy expected to grow by a sluggish 0.3% —and consumer spending inching up by a mere 1.3% . You can get a deeper look into these figures on UK e-commerce CAC trends on wearefounders.uk . UK E-commerce CAC Benchmarks by Industry To put this in perspective, here’s a quick look at the average Customer Acquisition Costs across different D2C sectors in the UK. The numbers highlight just how much financial pressure brands are under to make every marketing pound count. Industry Sector Average CAC (£) Fashion & Apparel £65 - £95 Health & Wellness £70 - £110 Home Goods £85 - £130 Food & Beverage £45 - £80 Beauty & Cosmetics £55 - £100 These figures aren’t just abstract numbers; they represent the real cost of getting a new customer through the door. When your CAC is this high, your margin for error is practically zero. The Root Causes of Rising CAC So, what’s actually driving these costs up? A few key factors are squeezing marketers from all sides, making efficient growth harder than ever. Getting a handle on these pressures is the first step toward building an acquisition strategy that can actually withstand them. Intensified Competition: It’s never been easier to launch an e-commerce store. That’s great for entrepreneurs but terrible for ad costs, as it floods every niche with competitors all bidding on the same keywords and chasing the same audiences. Ad Platform Saturation: The big platforms like Meta and Google are crowded, creating an auction environment that constantly drives ad prices higher. Simply reaching your ideal customer costs a lot more than it did just a few years ago. Economic Headwinds: With household budgets getting tighter, people are thinking twice before buying. They take longer to decide, which means you need more marketing touchpoints to get them across the line, pushing up the cost of a single sale. The core problem isn’t just that ad spend is rising; it’s the lack of a single, clear picture. When your Shopify data, ad platform metrics, and analytics all live in different places, it’s impossible to see what’s really going on and make smart, cost-saving decisions. Adopting a Full-Funnel Mindset The only sustainable way to cut your acquisition cost is to stop guessing and start analysing. A full-funnel approach means you connect the dots between every single stage of the customer journey. You need real answers to the big questions: “Which channels are bringing in customers with the highest lifetime value?” or “Where are the biggest drop-off points in my checkout process?” This is where modern analytics tools become non-negotiable. Instead of drowning in a dozen different dashboards, a platform like Menza cuts through the noise. It analyses all your data sources together and gives you clear, plain-English answers. This guide will walk you through a practical playbook to audit your data, optimise your entire funnel, and finally get your acquisition costs under control. Conducting a Ruthless Funnel and Data Audit Before you can fix your customer acquisition cost, you have to play detective. Your mission is to find all the hidden leaks in your funnel where you’re bleeding money, time, and potential customers. This isn’t about glancing at a few dashboards. It’s about a ruthless, top-to-bottom audit of your entire customer journey, from the first ad impression right through to the final thank-you page. A classic mistake is looking at data in silos. Your Meta Ads dashboard tells one story, Google Analytics tells another, and your Shopify backend tells a third. When these platforms aren’t talking to each other, you’re left with a fragmented picture. It’s impossible to find the real source of the problem or truly understand how much it costs to win a new customer. The goal here is to create a single source of truth. By connecting these disparate data sources, you can finally start asking the questions that actually matter and get answers you can trust. Mapping the Entire Customer Journey To find the leaks, you need a map. Start by sketching out every single touchpoint a potential customer has with your brand. Think visually. Trace their path from the moment they see an ad to the moment they complete a purchase. This map helps you identify the key conversion stages and, more importantly, the drop-off points. You need to know your numbers at each step to see where the biggest opportunities for improvement are hiding. Awareness: How many people are seeing your ads or organic content? What’s your click-through rate ( CTR )? Consideration: Once they land on your site, how many visit a product page? What’s the bounce rate? Conversion: What percentage of visitors add an item to their cart? And critically, how many of those actually complete the checkout? Retention: What’s the repeat purchase rate for customers acquired from different channels? The most expensive mistake is paying to acquire a customer only to lose them to a confusing website or a clunky checkout. Pinpointing these friction points is the fastest way to improve your marketing ROI. Asking the Right Questions Once you have a unified view of your data, you can move beyond surface-level metrics. A tool like Menza lets you ask specific, conversational questions and get immediate, data-backed answers—no technical expertise required. Instead of just staring at your overall CAC, you need to dig deeper. For a more detailed breakdown, check out our guide on how to measure marketing ROI effectively . Here are some of the critical questions you should be asking your data to uncover wastage: “What’s our conversion rate from add-to-cart to purchase on mobile versus desktop?” “Which marketing channel had the highest blended CAC over the last 30 days?” “Show me the customer journey for users who abandoned their cart after entering a discount code.” “What is the 60 -day LTV of customers we acquired from our latest TikTok campaign compared to our Google Ads campaign?” This common cycle of high ad spend and intense competition is what leads to stagnating acquisition costs. This visual really hammers home how simply throwing more budget at ads without fixing underlying funnel issues rarely leads to sustainable growth. In fact, it can quickly inflate your CAC. From Insights to Action An audit is only useful if it leads to action. Your findings should give you a clear, prioritised hit list of areas to fix. For example, if your audit reveals a massive drop-off between adding an item to the cart and starting the checkout, that’s your next focus. Is it a surprise shipping cost? Is the page loading too slowly on mobile? By identifying the exact problem, you can focus your resources on a solution that will have a direct impact. This data-first approach transforms your efforts from scattered guesswork into a targeted strategy designed to efficiently lower your customer acquisition cost. Refining Your Targeting and Supercharging Ad Creatives Once you’ve audited your funnel and know where the leaks are, the real work begins. It’s time to stop pouring money into ads that just aren’t pulling their weight. Spraying your budget across broad, generic audiences is one of the fastest ways I’ve seen brands burn through cash and inflate their acquisition costs. The fix is a two-pronged attack: sharpening your audience targeting to a razor’s edge and systematically levelling up your ad creatives. This is about moving from guesswork to data. Who is your ideal customer, really? Not who you think they are. Answering that question with hard numbers is the bedrock of any strategy to reduce customer acquisition cost . Pinpoint Your Most Profitable Customer Segments The most powerful insights you have are already sitting in your customer base. Stop relying on the generic personas ad platforms give you and start digging into the demographics, behaviours, and purchase histories of your highest-value customers. These are the people who buy again and again—the ones with the highest lifetime value (LTV). With a tool like Menza, you can uncover these segments just by asking plain-English questions. For example, a simple query like, “What are the common attributes of customers with an LTV over £500?” might instantly show you that your best buyers are in a specific age bracket, live in certain postcodes, and almost always purchase a particular product bundle. Armed with that knowledge, you can build lookalike audiences on platforms like Meta with incredible precision. You’re no longer guessing; you’re telling the algorithm to find more people who look exactly like your proven, most profitable customers. This alone can dramatically improve your chances of a lower-cost conversion. Exclude Underperforming Audiences Ruthlessly Just as critical as knowing who to target is knowing who not to target. Your audit probably flagged a few audience segments that love to click but never seem to convert. Or maybe they make one small purchase and then disappear forever. These are budget drains. You need to constantly monitor the performance of different audience groups and be absolutely ruthless about excluding the ones that don’t perform. This might be certain age groups, locations, or interests that consistently deliver a high cost-per-acquisition without a corresponding high LTV. Systematically cutting these segments from your campaigns is one of the most direct ways to make every pound you spend work harder. By focusing your budget on proven, high-performing segments and actively excluding the unprofitable ones, you shift from a scattergun approach to precision targeting. This simple change can have a massive impact on your overall CAC. Implement a Structured Creative Testing Framework Even with perfect targeting, a weak creative will fall flat. Your ad is your frontline soldier, and it needs to be effective. To supercharge your creative, you have to move away from random A/B tests and adopt a structured framework that produces consistent winners. Start by breaking your ads down into their core components and testing each one methodically. This is how you learn what actually resonates with your audience, element by element. The Hook: Test the first 1-3 seconds of your video or the main headline of an image ad. Does an outrageous claim grab more attention than a relatable problem? The Angle: A single product can be sold from dozens of angles. For a skincare brand, you could test a “scientific ingredients” angle against a “confidence-boosting results” angle. The Offer: Don’t just stick to one incentive. See how a “ 20% Off ” discount performs against a “ Free Shipping ” offer or a “ Buy One, Get One Free ” deal. The Call-to-Action (CTA): Test direct commands like “Shop Now” against softer, lower-commitment CTAs like “Learn More” to see which one drives the most qualified traffic. When you’re working on ad creative, learning how to craft compelling video hooks is a non-negotiable skill. That initial engagement is often what separates a winning ad from a dud. For a deeper look at applying these principles across your campaigns, check out our guide on how to build a full-funnel advertising strategy . Just how critical is this efficiency? Look at the UK e-commerce market. By 2025, benchmarks show massive differences between industries—electronics brands are paying £377 per customer, while arts and entertainment get by on a leaner £21 . The alarming part is that all sectors have seen acquisition costs jump by as much as 222% since 2013, as ad inflation and minimal 0.3% GDP growth squeeze everyone’s margins. The final piece of this puzzle is proactive monitoring. Don’t wait for your weekly report to find out your best-performing ad started fatiguing three days ago. An automated system like Menza can alert you the moment an ad’s performance dips below your threshold. This lets you swap in fresh creative before you’ve wasted any significant budget, turning creative management from a reactive chore into a strategic advantage. Optimising Your Landing Pages and Checkout Flow Even the most brilliant ads will fall flat if they lead to a frustrating website experience. You’ve already paid to get visitors to your site; now, the goal is to make it as easy as possible for them to convert. This is where optimising your landing pages and streamlining your checkout becomes a powerful lever to reduce customer acquisition cost . Improving your conversion rate means every pound spent on ads goes further. A small lift here can have a massive impact on your bottom line without you needing to spend a single extra penny on advertising. It’s about maximising the value of the traffic you already have. The journey from an ad click to a conversion is fragile. Any friction, confusion, or unexpected surprises can cause a potential customer to bail. That’s why a methodical approach to on-site optimisation is non-negotiable for sustainable growth. A/B Testing Your Critical Landing Page Elements Your landing page is your digital salesperson. Its one job is to convince the visitor to take the next step. Instead of making changes based on gut feelings, a structured A/B testing plan lets the data guide your decisions. Start by focusing on the elements with the biggest potential impact on a visitor’s decision-making process. Headlines: Does your headline match the promise made in the ad? Test a benefit-driven headline (e.g., “Get a Flawless Glow in 5 Minutes”) against a feature-focused one (e.g., “Our Vitamin C Serum with Hyaluronic Acid”). Calls-to-Action (CTAs): The smallest changes here can yield big results. Test the button colour, text (“Add to Basket” vs. “Buy It Now”), and placement to see what drives the most clicks. Social Proof: How you display customer trust matters. Test video testimonials against star ratings or user-generated photos to see which format resonates most with your audience. A common mistake is testing too many variables at once. To get clean, actionable data, isolate a single element—like the headline—and test two distinct versions against each other. This ensures you know exactly what caused the change in performance. Removing Friction from Your Checkout Process The checkout is the final hurdle, and it’s where an astonishing number of sales are lost. The average cart abandonment rate hovers around 70% . Think about that: seven out of ten potential customers who add items to their cart leave without buying. Every percentage point you can shave off that number directly lowers your effective CAC. Your primary goal should be making the checkout as seamless and transparent as possible. Common Checkout Conversion Killers Friction Point The Problem The Solution Forced Account Creation Customers hate being forced to create an account before they can buy. Offer a prominent guest checkout option. Surprise Shipping Costs Unexpected fees are the number one reason for cart abandonment. Display shipping costs upfront on the product or cart page. Limited Payment Options Not offering popular methods like PayPal or Apple Pay can deter users. Integrate a variety of trusted payment gateways. Complex Forms Asking for unnecessary information adds steps and frustration. Only ask for the essential details needed to fulfil the order. To find your specific friction points, you need to dig into your data. A platform like Menza allows you to ask direct questions, like, “What is our checkout abandonment rate by device?” If you discover mobile abandonment is significantly higher, that points to a specific problem with your mobile checkout experience that needs immediate attention. Proactive Monitoring to Catch Costly Glitches Technical issues can silently sabotage your conversion rates. A broken “Add to Cart” button or a malfunctioning payment gateway can go unnoticed for hours—or even days—wasting thousands in ad spend. This is where proactive monitoring becomes your safety net. Instead of manually checking your site, you can use an automated system to keep watch for you. For instance, you could set up an alert in Menza to notify you instantly if your site-wide conversion rate suddenly drops by more than 10% in an hour. This allows your team to react immediately, find the glitch, and fix it before it becomes an expensive disaster. This automated oversight transforms your approach from reactive problem-solving to proactive performance management, ensuring your optimised funnel stays that way. Boosting Retention to Increase Customer Lifetime Value The relentless chase for new customers often blinds brands to a far more powerful strategy for managing acquisition costs: making every customer you already have more valuable. Shifting your focus from pure acquisition to robust retention isn’t just a defensive move; it’s the ultimate offensive play in a competitive market. A high Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) gives your business the financial firepower to absorb higher acquisition costs and sustainably outspend rivals. When you know a customer is likely to spend more with you over time, you can justify a larger upfront investment to win their business. This fundamentally changes the economics of your marketing. Nail the Post-Purchase Experience The customer journey doesn’t end at checkout; that’s where the real relationship begins. A stellar post-purchase experience is what turns a one-time buyer into a loyal advocate. It’s your first and best chance to prove you value their business beyond the transaction. A simple, effective onboarding sequence can make all the difference. For a skincare brand, this could be a series of emails with tips on how to use their new products. For a tech gadget, it might be a quick video guide to a key feature. The goal is simple: ensure the customer gets immediate value from what they bought. Build Loyalty That Actually Lasts Once a customer has had a great first experience, you need to give them compelling reasons to come back. Loyalty programmes, when done right, are incredibly effective. They create a virtuous cycle where customers feel rewarded for their repeat business, which encourages even more. Consider these approaches to foster genuine loyalty: Tiered Rewards: Create a system where customers unlock better perks—like exclusive discounts or early access to new products—as they spend more. This gamifies the experience and provides a clear incentive to stick around. Exclusive Community Access: Offer your best customers a spot in a private group or forum. This builds a sense of belonging and transforms customers into a community that can provide priceless feedback. Surprise and Delight: Every so often, send a small, unexpected gift or a personalised discount to a loyal customer. These gestures can generate powerful word-of-mouth and strengthen their emotional connection to your brand. For UK D2C brands, this focus on retention is more critical than ever. In 2025, acquiring a new customer costs 5-25 times more than keeping an existing one, with the average e-commerce CAC climbing to £70 . Top-performing brands combat this by obsessing over service, knowing that loyal customers have repurchase rates of 60-70% , compared to just 20% for newcomers. Impact of Retention on Profitability The data consistently shows that even a tiny improvement in retention can have an outsized effect on your bottom line. It’s one of the highest-leverage activities a brand can focus on. Retention Rate Increase Average Impact on Profitability 5% 25% - 95% 10% 50% - 150%+ These figures, often cited in studies by firms like Bain & Company, highlight why the most resilient brands are retention-obsessed. The investment pays for itself many times over. You can explore more of these e-commerce benchmarks on LoyaltyLion . Proactive Service and Spotting Churn Risk This is where operational insights become a game-changer. Imagine getting an automated alert from a platform like Menza that one of your bestselling products is at risk of a stockout. This lets you act proactively—perhaps by notifying customers of a brief delay or suggesting a similar item—and prevent a poor experience that could lead to churn. The most powerful way to boost LTV is by identifying at-risk customers before they leave. By analysing purchase frequency and engagement data, you can spot customers who are showing signs of drifting away and launch targeted re-engagement campaigns to win them back. These campaigns don’t have to be complicated. It could be a simple “We miss you” email with a special offer or a survey asking for feedback. The key is to show them you’ve noticed they’re gone and that you value their business. For a more in-depth look at this crucial metric, check out our guide on how to calculate customer lifetime value . By making retention a core part of your growth engine, you build a more resilient, profitable business that can weather the rising tide of acquisition costs. Answering Your Top Questions About CAC As teams start getting serious about managing their ad spend, a few common questions always pop up. It’s natural when you’re shifting to a more data-driven approach. Think of this as your practical FAQ for moving forward—getting these answers right helps make sure the core concepts we’ve discussed really stick. Let’s tackle the most frequent ones I hear from brands trying to reduce customer acquisition cost . What Is a Good Customer Acquisition Cost for a UK E-commerce Brand? This is the million-pound question, isn’t it? The honest answer is: there’s no single number. A “good” CAC is completely relative to your industry, Average Order Value (AOV), and most importantly, your Customer Lifetime Value (LTV). What’s perfectly sustainable for one brand could be a total disaster for another. The gold standard metric you should be obsessing over is the LTV to CAC ratio . A healthy, sustainable business typically aims for a ratio of at least 3:1 . In simple terms, for every pound you spend to get a customer, they should generate at least three pounds in revenue over their lifetime with your brand. For example, if your average customer spends £300 over their lifetime, then a CAC of £100 or less is a solid target. Remember, UK benchmarks vary wildly—fashion might average around £129 while electronics can hit £377 . The key isn’t to chase some arbitrary industry number, but to relentlessly improve your own LTV:CAC ratio using the strategies in this guide. How Can I Calculate CAC Accurately Without Complex Spreadsheets? This is a massive pain point for so many brands, usually because their data is all over the place. The basic formula—Total Marketing & Sales Spend ÷ Number of New Customers Acquired—looks simple on paper but gets messy fast. Your “total spend” is often fragmented across Google Ads, Meta, SEO agencies, influencer payments, and who knows what else. Manually pulling that from a dozen sources and wrestling with spreadsheets is where things break down. This is where modern analytics tools become indispensable. Instead of all that manual work, a platform can connect directly to all your data streams. It automatically adds up every relevant cost and correctly attributes new customers. With an integrated system, you eliminate the manual data wrangling and human error that plague spreadsheet-based analysis. You get a single, trustworthy figure for your blended CAC, updated in real time. This simple shift means you can spend your time acting on the numbers, not just trying to find them. How Can a Small Non-Technical Team Implement These Strategies? This is one of the most common and valid concerns I hear. Most growing businesses don’t have a dedicated data analyst, and the idea of implementing a complex data strategy feels completely overwhelming. The solution is to find tools built specifically for non-technical users. The old way required knowing SQL or how to build complicated dashboards from scratch. title: Hack to Hire Episode 2: Turning Real-World Business Friction into AI-Driven Workflows
summary: What happens when AI meets real business pressure? Hack to Hire episode 2 explores real-world systems, diving into prototype details and their implications for enterprise workflows.
body_text: Hack to Hire 2 has concluded earlier, but the use cases developed during the event continue to stand out. Rather than focusing on experimental models or theoretical benchmarks, the hackathon produced concrete system designs that address persistent business challenges across supply chains, retail operations, and document-heavy industries. Built within a limited timeframe, these projects demonstrated how AI when paired with the right infrastructure and system architecture can be embedded directly into operational workflows. In the following article, we will take a closer look at these prototype cases and further explore their practical applications and value. Decision-makers must continuously assess compliance, performance, and risk across a large and evolving supplier base. However, relevant data is often distributed across internal records, supplier submissions, external documents, and public news sources. Technical & Business Challenges The primary challenge lies in fragmentation. Supplier information exists in multiple formats and systems, making it difficult to establish a unified, up-to-date view. As a result, sustainability compliance checks and quality assessments are largely manual, delaying critical decisions and increasing operational risk. Solution Architecture The proposed solution consolidates supplier data, documents, and external information through a centralized data pipeline. Within the system architecture, Bitdeer AI Cloud provides the virtual machine environment and data processing layer used to run ETL workflows, host the analytical dashboard, and support AI-driven insight generation. Structured data is stored centrally, while AI models analyze supplier attributes to produce quality scores and contextual recommendations. The dashboard presents these insights in a unified view, enabling more informed and timely supplier management decisions Outcome The prototype illustrates how AI-supported analytics can transform supplier evaluation from manual reviews into a more systematic and insight-driven process, particularly valuable for sustainability-focused supply chains. Use Case 2: Retail Store Intelligence for Planogram Execution Background Retail ground staff spend significant time executing product placement according to predefined planograms. Store managers must oversee large teams, while brand and product managers often lack direct visibility into how products are ultimately displayed on the shop floor. Challenges Manual reporting and visual checks are time-consuming and inconsistent. Solution Architecture The system digitizes the planogram workflow from instruction to verification. Product placement requirements are recorded and distributed to ground staff via a centralized interface. After execution, staff upload photos through a mobile web browser. The results are automatically recorded and aggregated, allowing managers to review execution status and performance without manual follow-up. Outcome By combining visual evidence with automated reporting, the solution improves transparency across retail operations and reduces the manual burden on both frontline staff and management. Use Case 3: Automated Tender Document Intelligence for SMEs Background Singapore’s construction industry issues thousands of government tenders each year, many consisting of hundreds of pages of documentation. For SMEs, participating in these tenders is critical but resource-intensive. Challenges Tender documents are typically received via email and reviewed manually. Processing a single tender can take several days, placing heavy strain on small quality assurance teams and increasing the risk of missed deadlines or errors. Solution Architecture The proposed pipeline automates tender intake and evaluation. Incoming emails trigger document processing workflows that extract, analyze, and assess tender requirements. AI and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques reference internal document repositories such as certificates and project histories to perform eligibility checks.
